title: A machine-learning-assisted TESS search confirms a previously unknown hot Jupiter
summary: The T16 pipeline processed 83.7 million TESS Cycle 1 full-frame-image light curves and reported 10,091 new transiting-planet candidates, alongside previously known candidates. Radial-velocity follow-up confirmed TIC 183374187 b as a newly identified hot Jupiter, demonstrating that the semi-automated search yielded at least one bona fide new planet. Most entries in the catalog remain candidates rather than confirmed planets.
ai_technology: T16 semi-automated transit search with random-forest machine-learning vetting

evidence.tested: The T16 pipeline processed 83.7 million TESS Cycle 1 full-frame-image light curves and reported 10,091 new transiting-planet candidates, alongside previously known candidates.
evidence.unknown: The 10,091 entries are planet candidates, most unconfirmed. The cited discovery claim here is limited to TIC 183374187 b, which the authors say was confirmed with radial-velocity follow-up; the pipeline is described as machine-learning-assisted, not fully autonomous.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning-assisted pipeline classified light curves and prioritized possible transit signals; human vetting and Magellan/PFS radial-velocity observations confirmed the highlighted planet.
